bank.question: A Saudi finance company and a bank both adopt SAMA's Cyber Security Framework. Which statement about domain applicability is accurate for the bank?
options: Only the governance domain applies to the bank
All domains of the framework apply to the bank
The bank may exclude the e-banking subdomain
The bank applies only controls it chooses to self-assess
bank.explanation: The framework states that all domains apply to the banking sector; exclusions in section 1.4 are for other financial institutions.

bank.question: Rimal Bank's committee charter states members 'meet when needed'. A reviewer flags it. What is the most likely reason?
options: The charter must require weekly meetings chaired by the CEO
Charters may not mention meeting frequency at all
Only SAMA may decide when the committee meets
The charter must set a meeting frequency of at least quarterly
bank.explanation: Section 3.1.1 requires the charter to reflect objectives, roles, minimum participants and a meeting frequency of at least quarterly.

bank.question: Internal audit asks to be a full voting member of the cyber security committee. What does the framework provide?
options: Internal audit may attend as an observer
Internal audit must chair the committee
Internal audit must not attend at all
Internal audit votes only on budget items
bank.explanation: The framework lists internal audit as an optional observer, keeping its independence to audit cyber security later.

bank.question: Which body endorses the cyber security strategy and policy after the cyber security committee has approved them?
options: The chief information officer
SAMA's IT risk supervision team
The board of directors
The external auditor
bank.explanation: Section 3.1.4 gives the board ultimate responsibility, including endorsing governance, strategy and policy after committee approval.

bank.question: Rimal Bank's awareness programme is written, approved and monitored with KPIs, but nobody measures whether it reduces risk. Which maturity level has it reached, and what would level 4 add?
options: Level 4; level 5 adds a written policy
Level 2; level 3 adds KRIs and peer comparison
Level 3; level 4 adds effectiveness measurement using KRIs
Level 5; nothing more is needed
bank.explanation: Defined, approved, implemented and monitored controls with KPIs are level 3. Level 4 adds periodic measurement of effectiveness using KRIs.

bank.question: Which of these is a responsibility of senior management under section 3.1.4?
options: Making sure cyber duties are written into job descriptions of key positions and cyber staff
Performing cyber security audits
Approving the cyber committee charter
Running the security operations centre each night
bank.explanation: Senior management ensures staff accept and comply with the policy and that cyber responsibilities appear in job descriptions. Audits belong to internal audit; charter approval to the board.

bank.question: A board member says the board can hand cyber security entirely to the committee and stop worrying about it. How should the CISO respond?
options: The board may transfer all responsibility to the committee by resolution
Responsibility passes to SAMA once the self-assessment is filed
Responsibility passes to the CISO once SAMA gives its no objection
The board may delegate tasks, but it keeps ultimate responsibility for cyber security
bank.explanation: The framework says ultimate responsibility rests with the board; it can delegate cyber responsibilities to a committee but remains accountable.

bank.question: Under the framework's documentation model, which document defines 'what' controls apply, such as password rules and logging?
options: The cyber security policy
Cyber security standards
Cyber security procedures
The cyber security strategy
bank.explanation: Standards set what controls must be implemented and act as baselines; the policy says why, and procedures say how.

bank.question: A third-party call-centre agency answers Rimal Bank's customers. Does section 3.1.6 expect its agents to be covered by the awareness programme?
options: Yes, the programme must cover third parties as well as staff and customers
No, only the bank's direct employees are covered
Only if the agency is based outside Saudi Arabia
Only if the agency asks to be included
bank.explanation: Section 3.1.6 requires the programme to be defined and conducted for staff, third parties and customers.

bank.question: The awareness team plans to send one identical email to tellers, developers and corporate clients. Which section 3.1.6 requirement does this weaken?
options: Reporting the programme to SAMA every month
Limiting awareness to employees in head office
Tailoring the programme to different target groups through multiple channels
Running awareness only at induction
bank.explanation: The framework asks the programme to target behaviours by tailoring it to different audiences through multiple channels.

bank.question: Which of the following is part of the minimum content of the cyber awareness programme?
options: The bank's annual profit forecast
Details of individual staff disciplinary cases
The source code of the bank's applications
The roles and responsibilities regarding cyber security
bank.explanation: Minimum content is an explanation of security measures, roles and responsibilities, and relevant emerging threats.

bank.question: Staff who carry out cyber risk assessments at Rimal Bank have had no training since joining. Which section is most directly breached?
options: Section 3.1.2, alignment with the sector strategy
Section 3.1.7, specialist skills training for staff involved in risk assessments
Section 3.4.2, approval of material outsourcing
Section 3.3.11, secure disposal of assets
bank.explanation: Section 3.1.7 lists staff involved in risk assessments among those who need specialist or security-related skills training.

bank.question: Which HR-process requirement in section 3.3.1 continues after an employee leaves the bank?
options: Monthly awareness emails to former staff
Annual background checks on former staff
Access to the bank's systems for a handover year
Non-disclosure clauses in staff agreements that apply during and after employment
bank.explanation: Section 3.3.1 requires cyber responsibilities and non-disclosure clauses in staff agreements during and after employment, and revoking access on exit.

bank.question: The CIO asks whether the IT training plan can be produced every three years to save effort. What does the IT Governance Framework say?
options: An IT training plan must be developed annually and reviewed periodically
A plan every three years is acceptable if SAMA is told
No training plan is needed if staff hold certifications
The plan is optional for banks with fewer than 100 IT staff
bank.explanation: Section 3.1.8 requires an annual IT training plan, reviewed periodically, plus formal training for IT staff and contractors.

bank.question: Under section 3.1.8 of the IT Governance Framework, what must banks identify for staff in critical IT roles?
options: The salary band for each critical role
The personal social media accounts of role holders
The professional certifications those roles require
A SAMA-approved deputy for every role
bank.explanation: Banks must identify and define critical IT roles and the professional certifications required for them.

bank.question: Rimal Bank's security operations centre runs 24x7 but analysts have had no training since they were hired. Which requirement is unmet?
options: SOC staff must rotate into branches each year
SOC staff must be skilled and continuously trained
SOC staff must be employed by SAMA
SOC staff must hold a credit adviser certificate
bank.explanation: Section 3.3.14 lists skilled and continuously trained staff among the requirements for security event management.

bank.question: Which statement best describes SAMA's business continuity framework's view of awareness and training, in general terms?
options: Only the IT department needs to know about continuity plans
Suppliers must never be told about the bank's continuity plans
Continuity training replaces cyber awareness training
Staff and relevant suppliers should know the continuity plans, their roles and their BCM contact, with training for BCM staff
bank.explanation: The BCM framework calls for a training and awareness programme so staff and relevant third parties know the plans, their roles and their contact, with training for those involved in BCM.

bank.question: An email to Rimal Bank's chief financial officer appears to come from a regulator and asks her to open an attached 'inspection notice'. Which threat named in SAMA's framework does this match?
options: Shoulder surfing at a branch counter
Card skimming at an ATM
Whaling, a targeted attack on a senior executive
Batch processing failure
bank.explanation: Whaling targets senior executives with tailored messages; the framework names it with spear-phishing as an awareness topic.

bank.question: Under the Counter-Fraud Framework, which group is specifically named for specialised fraud training because of the risk of their role?
options: Customer-facing staff in branches
Staff on long-term leave
Shareholders of the bank
Customers who hold savings accounts only
bank.explanation: Section 4.3.1 gives managers with authority, customer-facing branch staff, staff operating counter-fraud controls and investigators as examples needing specialised training.

bank.question: What does the Counter-Fraud Framework require an SMS one-time password to state?
options: The customer's full account balance
The purpose, amount and merchant name, in the customer's chosen language
The customer's national ID number
The name of the bank employee who sent it
bank.explanation: Section 4.4 requires the purpose, amount and merchant name to be clearly defined, in the language selected on the account.

bank.question: A customer changes the mobile number on his account at an ATM. What alert does the Cyber Security Framework require?
options: An email to the branch manager only
A letter to the customer's home within 30 days
No alert, because the ATM verified the PIN
An SMS alert sent to both the old and the new mobile numbers
bank.explanation: Section 3.3.13 requires an SMS to both the old and new numbers when the mobile number changes.

bank.question: Rimal Bank's fraud team and cyber team never share data and run separate incident responses. Which Counter-Fraud Framework principle is weakest?
options: Remote account opening controls
Third-party fraud awareness
Alignment of fraud, financial crime and cyber capabilities
Supervisory notifications
bank.explanation: Section 4.5 requires defined roles, cross training, joint task forces, shared threat intelligence and aligned incident response across the three teams.

bank.question: Which activity does the Counter-Fraud Framework list as high-risk, needing multi-factor authentication before it is acted on?
options: Adding or modifying beneficiaries
Viewing the branch opening hours
Reading a product brochure in the app
Checking the exchange rate page
bank.explanation: Section 4.4 lists adding or modifying beneficiaries among high-risk activities, along with new device logins and password resets.

bank.question: SAMA's April 2022 urgent measures followed a rise in which threat, according to SAMA's announcement?
options: Ransomware attacks that encrypted bank data centres
Physical robberies of cash-in-transit vehicles
Insider trading in bank shares
Fraudulent websites and social media accounts used in social-engineering scams
bank.explanation: SAMA cited a notable rise in fraudulent websites and social media accounts and recurring social-engineering scams that led customers to reveal passwords and codes.

bank.question: What did SAMA do on 12 April 2022 after re-evaluating its urgent anti-fraud measures?
options: Made the SAR 60,000 limit permanent for all customers
Restored the earlier daily limit and allowed remote account opening again
Banned remote account opening for a year
Closed online banking during weekends
bank.explanation: SAMA raised the daily limit back to its previous ceiling (customers could lower it) and brought back remote account opening under standard procedures.

bank.question: A branch employee's fraud training records cannot be found. Which Counter-Fraud Framework requirement is at risk?
options: Keeping records of fraud training delivered and awareness activity
Publishing training records on the bank's website
Sending training records to customers
Deleting training records after each campaign
bank.explanation: Section 4.3.1 requires banks to maintain records of fraud training delivered to employees and awareness activity conducted.

bank.question: Customer fraud awareness at Rimal Bank is sent once, at onboarding. Which Counter-Fraud Framework expectation does this miss?
options: Awareness must be delivered only in branches
Awareness should cover the whole customer lifecycle and reflect current fraud trends
Awareness should be limited to corporate clients
Awareness must be approved by SAMA before sending
bank.explanation: Section 4.3.2 asks for timely, trend-based awareness across the customer lifecycle through all channels, with extra support for vulnerable customers.

bank.question: Which statement about SAMA's 2021 control and awareness measures for branch and customer service employees is accurate?
options: They replace the Cyber Security Framework for branch staff
They apply only to banks with more than 50 branches
They are guidance that banks may ignore
They are minimum requirements and do not replace the Cyber Security and BCM frameworks
bank.explanation: The measures say they represent minimum requirements and apply without prejudice to related rules, including the Cyber Security and BCM frameworks.

bank.question: A teller wants to copy a customer list to a USB stick to work from home. What do the 2021 measures require?
options: Copying is allowed if the file is renamed
Copying or sharing data needs the consent of an authorised person
Copying is allowed for staff above a set job grade
Copying is allowed after working hours only
bank.explanation: The measures forbid copying or sharing data or installing software without the consent of the authorised person.

bank.question: A network engineer needs access to a branch's systems for maintenance. What do the 2021 measures say about his access?
options: Give full access so he can test every screen
Give him the branch manager's login for the day
Limit it to network maintenance, without access to confidential customer information
Give access only if a customer is present
bank.explanation: Access for IT and support staff is limited to network maintenance without access to customers' confidential information.

bank.question: Rimal Bank lets tellers log in from branch computers at midnight with no extra checks. Which control is missing?
options: Restricting branch access to banking systems after working hours, with controlled exceptions
Hiding customer signatures on active accounts
Changing passwords every three months
Testing staff every six months
bank.explanation: The measures require restricting access from branch computers after official working hours and setting precautionary controls when access is needed.

bank.question: What must banks do with customer signatures and balances on unclaimed or abandoned accounts?
options: Show them only to the branch manager
Publish them in a dormant-account list
Hide them for all such accounts
Delete them after one year
bank.explanation: The measures require hiding customer signatures and balances for all accounts in an unclaimed or abandoned state.

bank.question: A branch runs its information security and fraud campaign every quarter but has never tested staff. What does SAMA require?
options: Tests only when SAMA visits the branch
Tests once every two years by internal audit
No tests, because campaigns are enough
Tests and surveys at least every six months to measure the campaigns' effectiveness
bank.explanation: Point 6 of the awareness procedures requires tests and surveys at least every six months to assess the three-monthly campaigns.

bank.question: Under the Cyber Security Framework, who should start access changes when a teller moves from Jeddah to a head office role?
options: The teller herself, by email to IT
The human resources department, as part of joiner-mover-leaver management
The customer service supervisor at the new site
SAMA's IT risk supervision team
bank.explanation: Section 3.3.5 says changes in job status or position for internal staff should be instigated by HR, with formal approval and timely processing.

bank.question: What did SAMA's December 2021 circular ask financial institutions to do about the Personal Data Protection Law?
options: Align internal policies, carry out a gap analysis and give the board a time-bound correction plan
Appoint SAMA as the bank's data protection officer
Stop all data sharing with government bodies
Move all customer data outside the Kingdom
bank.explanation: The circular required review of policies against the PDPL and SDAIA rules, a gap analysis, and a timeline plan presented to the board for approval.

bank.question: Rimal Bank plans to outsource its card processing. When should the cyber risk assessment be done?
options: After the contract has run for one year
Only if an incident occurs at the provider
When the outsourcing is being considered, before the decision is final
At the next scheduled internal audit
bank.explanation: Section 3.2.1 says the risk process should start when outsourcing is considered, as well as early in projects and before critical changes.

bank.question: Who must accept and endorse the results of a cyber risk assessment under section 3.2.1?
options: The relevant business owner, as risk owner
The external auditor
The most junior analyst involved
The vendor that supplied the system
bank.explanation: Results are reported to the relevant business owner, the risk owner, who should accept and endorse them.

bank.question: A cyber risk is to be transferred to an insurer. What does the framework require for transfer to be valid?
options: SAMA must sign the insurance contract
The CISO must pay the premium personally
The risk must first be published to customers
The receiving provider accepts the risk and the transfer actually takes place
bank.explanation: Section 3.2.1.3 says transfer involves sharing the risk with a provider, acceptance by that provider and the actual transfer.

bank.question: Which statement about the threat intelligence process in section 3.3.16 is accurate?
options: It relies only on vendor marketing material
It uses internal and external sources and shares relevant intelligence with stakeholders such as SAMA
It must be kept secret from SAMA
It replaces the vulnerability management process
bank.explanation: The process uses internal sources (logs, fraud, audit) and external ones (SAMA, government, forums), analyses them and shares intelligence with stakeholders.

bank.question: During a high incident, Rimal Bank's team overwrites server logs while restoring service quickly. Which incident management requirement did they ignore?
options: Annual penetration testing
Protection of relevant evidence and logs
Approval of the IT budget
Quarterly committee meetings
bank.explanation: Section 3.3.15 requires protecting relevant evidence and logs so forensics and root-cause analysis are possible.

bank.question: After a medium cyber incident, which order of reporting to SAMA reflects the framework?
options: A formal report first, then a phone call after one month
Only an annual summary of all incidents
Notification only if customers complain
Immediate notification, then a formal report once operations resume
bank.explanation: Section 3.3.15 requires immediate notification for medium or high incidents, then a formal report after operations resume.

bank.question: A SAMA reviewer asks for proof that branch staff awareness works. Which evidence best answers the question?
options: Six-monthly test and survey results compared with campaign topics and incidents
Attendance sheets from the induction day only
The bank's marketing brochures for customers
A list of posters displayed in branches
bank.explanation: The 2021 measures and section 3.1.6 both focus on effectiveness: six-monthly tests and surveys, analysed against campaigns, show whether behaviour changed.

bank.question: Rimal Bank's cyber incident team includes the CERT, but there is no repository of past incidents. Which requirement is missing?
options: A SAMA-approved press office
A separate CERT building in each region
A cyber security incident repository
A customer vote on incident priorities
bank.explanation: Section 3.3.15 lists establishing a cyber security incident repository among the process requirements, alongside root-cause analysis and improvement reports.
